A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CyclePrefDB/CycleReward work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–F. Equations, tables and figures can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, best-of-N experiments, DPO results, ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally displays DeCapBench score-component results.

M1.justification: The cycle-consistency preferences, BLIP-based reward model, pairwise losses and DPO procedures are retained. Corrected decoder assignments in Section 3.2 agree with v1's equations and decoder ablations; they do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same datasets and task coverage, including DCI/sDCI, detailed captioning, text-to-image generation, general VQA and Winoground. Appendix caption-length, hallucination and image-resolution scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain CLIPScore, VQAScore, HPSv2, PickScore, ImageReward, raw cycle consistency and IRDB-Cycle, alongside the same DPO comparators. The added SelfEval citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, sampling budgets and training settings remain unchanged, including the 250-caption and 100-image best-of-N pools. The new DeCapBench plots report components of the already described DCScore evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 9 supplies separate comprehensiveness and non-hallucination curves for DeCapBench, supporting a trade-off discussed without this plot in v1. Existing objective, dataset-size and filtering ablations move to Appendix E.4; failure analyses are retained in E.6.

E5.justification: Seed and repeated-evaluation information is retained, including three generation seeds during dataset construction and five GPT-4o evaluations for DrawBench/PartiPrompts. The additional component plots follow the existing error-bar presentation without introducing a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and Figure 3 retain their results. v2 adds Figure 9 component curves and corrects Appendix F's negative caption-length correlation attribution from CycleReward-I2T to CycleReward-T2I. Figure 4 loses the wooden-letter and cat-socks examples, while Figure 10 corrects a teapot prompt to match the retained ship images.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, preference and loss definitions, the shared-distribution assumption and Appendix A's pointwise-mutual-information derivation are mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction's ablation contribution drops the reference to text-to-image decoders, retaining the claim about stronger image-to-text language models. The central dataset, reward-model, performance and DPO claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 elaborates the comprehensiveness-versus-accuracy trade-off across reward variants and explicitly extends the discussion to CLIPScore. Existing reconstruction, token-limit, model-bias, domain-mismatch and aesthetic limitations are relocated rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the swapped backward-decoder descriptions: Stable Diffusion 3 reconstructs images for image-to-text preferences, and LLaVA-1.5-13B reconstructs text for text-to-image preferences. Hyperparameters, hardware, filtering thresholds and release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Rambhatla and Misra's SelfEval citation and removes Li et al.'s Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models. The principal positioning against human-preference metrics and direct cycle-consistency scoring is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction is reframed around measuring alignment, prose and headings are tightened, and existing ablation and limitations passages move into Appendices E.4 and E.6. The overall section sequence and scientific narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 4 is shortened and moved earlier, and the DeCapBench component figure is added. Qualitative displays receive formatting corrections, while the failure figure and ablation table move to the appendix; most displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 improves consistency by correcting decoder assignments, the mismatched Figure 10 prompt and the caption-length correlation attribution. Figure 9 provides useful evidence for the existing accuracy/detail discussion. These gains outweigh the modest loss of illustrative DPO examples; the method and principal empirical evidence remain unchanged.
